page.overview:
What is Simbelmynë?

Simbelmynë, also called Evermind and initially named Alfirin, was a white flower of Arda, known for its significance in Rohan.

Upon Tuor's arrival in Gondolin, he found these flowers and named them uilos. These flowers also grew on Elendil's tomb on Amon Anwar, and were there called alfirin. Later, in the Third Age, simbelmynë, as the Rohirrim called it, grew notably on the graves of the Kings of Rohan outside Edoras, and most abundantly on the burial mound of Helm Hammerhand.

The Elf Legolas used the same term alfirin (and mallos) to refer to an apparently different type of flower, described as "golden bells", found in Lebennin in Gondor.

Simbelmynë is an Old English term which means "ever-mind", and was the term used commonly in Rohan. The Elves called the same flower uilos ("snow white") and alfirin ("not mortal").
